items.title: How General Motors Could Win Big in the US Defense Missile Push
items.summary: GM has started making Patriot missile parts for Lockheed Martin as the Pentagon seeks to restock its inventory.

items.title: US to Sell F-35s to Saudi Arabia in $24.3 Billion Deal
items.summary: The State Department notified Congress that it plans to sell Saudi Arabia up to 48 F-35 warplanes in a first-time sale that could be worth as much as $24.3 billion. The sale of the Lockheed Martin Corp. fighter jet to Saudi Arabia has been in the works for a number of years. President Donald Trump signaled in November the US would sell F-35s to the Kingdom, offering Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman a prize he's long cherished, ahead of a visit to the White House that month. Meantime, the Pentagon and Lockheed Martin Corp. are moving to speed up the production of a new classified air-to-air missile for US Air Force and Navy jets that's seen as vital to deterring China. For more, we speak with Wayne Sanders, Senior Defense Research Analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence.

items.title: U.S. approves possible $24.3 billion F-35 sale to Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Investing.com -- The U.S. State Department has approved a possible $24.3 billion foreign military sale to Saudi Arabia that would include 48 F-35 Lightning II fighter jets, strengthening Riyadh’s air capabilities and interoperability with U.S. and allied forces.

items.title: US Department Of State Signs $24.3B Deal With Saudi Arabia To Sell F-35 Fighter Jets, But LMT Stock Slips
items.summary: The U.S. State Department has formally notified Congress of its intent to sell up to 48 F-35 stealth fighters to Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Patriot Missile Sprint Is Running Ahead of Plan, CEO Says
items.summary: Lockheed Martin’s CEO said the weapons maker was running ahead of schedule on its plan to more than triple production of sorely needed Patriot missiles.  The massive orders will change the share of revenue that the company generates from missile sales, Taiclet said Thursday.

items.title: GM to Produce Patriot Missile Parts as U.S. Faces Critical Arms Shortage
items.summary: The Detroit automaker’s partnership with Lockheed Martin is a potential lift to America’s munitions supplies depleted by the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East.

items.title: GM delivers first components for US interceptor missiles
items.summary: General Motors has delivered its first components for Lockheed Martin interceptor missiles as the defense contractor boosts production to rebuild US stocks in the middle of the Iran war and to meet international demand, Lockheed said Thursday."This extraordinary 22‑day turnaround underscores Lockheed Martin's relentless focus on execution -- delivering for our troops faster, with greater capacity," said Tim Cahill, president of Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control.
